//: This directory only. It declares what these files already are — ES modules — so that Vite's
config loader stops reporting them as CommonJS carrying ESM syntax.
All three packages' vitest.config.ts reach determinism.ts through their own
tests/determinism.ts re-export, which pulls a REPO-ROOT file into the config bundle. The root
package.json has no "type", so Vite classified these as CommonJS and printed a
configLoader: 'native' incompatibility notice on every test gate. Vite's only other lever is
VITE_CONFIG_NATIVE_IGNORE_WARNING, which suppresses the message rather than answering it, and
scripts/ci/report.mjs counts that notice into warnings.compiler, which is ratcheted at zero.
SCOPED HERE, NEVER AT THE ROOT. Adding "type": "module" to the root package.json was tried
and is measurably wrong: Playwright loads e2e/*.ts through a CommonJS require path and those
files use __dirname deliberately (see the note above A11Y_SCAN_REPORT in e2e/helpers.ts, cited by symbol because a line number in that file went stale in a single round), so e2e and a11y both
died with 'ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined in ES module scope'; and CodeQL's own
vendored parser wrapper is a CommonJS .js file under .cache/, which the root package scope
reaches, so sast died with 'exports is not defined in ES module scope' as well.
THREE CommonJS callers import this directory across that boundary, and all three are exercised
by the e2e and a11y gates on every push: playwright.config.ts:6 (the CONFIG load, whose failure
shape is the silent 'No tests found'), e2e/helpers.ts:5, and e2e/start-server.ts:5.
THE INVARIANT THAT ARRANGEMENT DEPENDS ON: NO FILE IN THIS DIRECTORY MAY TAKE A TOP-LEVEL
AWAIT. require() of an ES module works only while the module graph is synchronous, and one
top-level await here breaks all three callers above, which means the e2e and a11y gates.
THE FAILURE IS MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED, and it is not the identifier this note used to name.
Playwright's own loader transpiles the required file to CommonJS, so with a throwaway file in
this directory and a throwaway config importing it the run dies as
SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions and the top level bodies of modules
out of Node's CommonJS loader, at exit 1, behind a warning advising that "type": "module" be
set in the nearest package.json. It is already set, on the last line of this file, so that
advice is the wrong fix and the misdirection is the real cost of the mistake.
ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE is what the plain-Node require path reports instead, confirmed with
a control outside this repository. s3Server.ts, which stands a container up, is where
somebody will reach for a top-level await.
IT IS PINNED NOW, which this paragraph used to say it was not. Two tests in
packages/server/tests/gate-surface.test.ts parse every .ts file in this directory with the
TypeScript compiler API and fail on an await expression, a for-await loop or an await using
declaration that sits outside every function; a second one asserts that the two files a
CommonJS caller actually reaches, determinism.ts and s3Server.ts, import nothing but node:
builtins and relative paths that stay inside the scanned set, because Node's rule is about
the whole module graph and not about one directory's syntax.
Keep this note clear of gate-marker vocabulary. Every **/package.json is an integrity-scan
gate file, where a forbidden marker has no ledgerable exception, and this path is also read
as a test path, so the skip and sleep rules apply to it as well.
